data.one_liner: Flutter desktop library for managing multiple OS windows from a single engine and isolate.
data.what_it_does: Allows managing multiple OS windows for macOS, Windows, and Linux from a single Flutter engine and Dart isolate using the multi-view API. Inter-window communication uses plain Dart objects without serialization or native bridges.
use_when: Building a multi-window desktop application in Flutter
Sharing state and Dart objects directly between different app windows without IPC
Optimizing resource usage by avoiding multiple Flutter engine instances
avoid_when: Developing for mobile or web platforms
Needing separate isolates or engines per window
strengths: Windows share a single engine, isolate, and memory space
Direct Dart object sharing without serialization or isolate ports
Synchronous FFI-based native window chrome calls in 2.0
weaknesses: Requires manual modifications to native runner code for Linux and Windows
Popup positioning has limitations on Wayland Linux compositors
data.setup_notes: Requires manual platform-specific setup inside C++ files for Linux and Windows (e.g., updating application activation, dart project preparation, and window creation code).
